original_question: On the Bryant-Salamon G2-manifold R^4 x S^3, Proposition 6 gives a local 1-parameter family of SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons with gauge group SU(2) that extend smoothly over the singular orbit on the bundle P_id, and Theorem 5 shows that the member with parameter y_0 = 0 extends globally. Do any of the other local instantons from that family, namely those with y_0 != 0, also extend globally, and if they do, is their curvature necessarily unbounded at infinity?
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, open problem (e): whether the local G2-instantons on P_id from Proposition 6 with nonzero parameter y_0 extend globally on the Bryant-Salamon G2-manifold R^4 x S^3, and, if they do, whether their curvature is unbounded at infinity.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's own concrete formulation. It correctly identifies the ambient Bryant-Salamon manifold R^4 x S^3, the relevant local 1-parameter family from Proposition 6, the bundle P_id, the distinguished globally extending case y_0 = 0 from Theorem 5, and the two issues the paper isolates: global extendability for the remaining members of the family and possible curvature blow-up at infinity.
missing_details: The nearest official target in the paper is not a proved theorem or conjecture, but the explicit open problem stated in Section 3.3(e).
The local instantons are defined only in a neighbourhood of the singular orbit S^3; 'extend globally' means extend as G2-instantons over all of the Bryant-Salamon manifold R^4 x S^3.
Proposition 6 adds that these SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant local solutions are actually SU(2)^3-invariant, which is part of the exact scope.
The parameter space is all real y_0, and the problem concerns every nonzero real parameter y_0.
The bundle should be identified explicitly as P_id = SU(2)^2 x_{(Delta SU(2), id)} SU(2) over the singular orbit, as introduced in equation (3.27) and used in Lemma 2.

The family in question is the specific invariant family arising from the Proposition 5 ansatz together with the P_id smooth-extension conditions from Lemma 2, not arbitrary local instantons near the singular orbit.

To make the last clause fully stand-alone, 'curvature unbounded at infinity' should be understood as the pointwise norm |F_A|, measured with the Bryant-Salamon metric, being unbounded along the unique noncompact end; the paper does not add an extra decay or L^2 hypothesis to this Section 3.3(e) question.
refined_question: Let A_{y_0} be the 1-parameter family from Proposition 6 of SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant, in fact SU(2)^3-invariant, G2-instantons with gauge group SU(2), defined in a neighbourhood of the singular orbit S^3 in the Bryant-Salamon G2-manifold R^4 x S^3 and extending smoothly over S^3 on the bundle P_id = SU(2)^2 x_{(Delta SU(2), id)} SU(2). Theorem 5 shows that the member A_0 extends to a global G2-instanton on all of R^4 x S^3. For each nonzero real parameter y_0, does the corresponding local instanton A_{y_0} extend to a global G2-instanton on R^4 x S^3? If such a global extension exists, must its curvature norm |F_{A_{y_0}}| be unbounded along the noncompact end, i.e. at infinity?
justification: This matches the paper's narrowest official formulation: the concrete open problem in Section 3.3(e). Proposition 6 provides the local 1-parameter family on P_id, Theorem 5 identifies the y_0 = 0 member that extends globally, and Section 3.3(e) then asks whether any of the remaining y_0 != 0 local instantons also extend globally, adding the numerical suggestion that any such global solutions would have unbounded curvature at infinity. Your draft already captures that almost exactly; the refinement only makes explicit the exact symmetry class, bundle, quantifier on y_0, and the meanings of global extension and curvature unboundedness.
